TECH-08:
1. If no homepage was fetched → UNKNOWN.
2. Score = 50 (if HTTPS) + 50 (if viewport tag with 'width' present).
3. Cap score at 80 if the HTML contains both 'min-width:' and '1200px' (a weak signal of a fixed-width layout that may overflow on mobile).
TECH-09:
1. If there are no pages to compare → UNKNOWN.
2. Per page, Ratio = Raw words ÷ Rendered words × 100 (0 if rendered word count is 0).
3. Score = min(100, average ratio across all checked pages).
TECH-10:
1. If no headings were found on any page → Score = 0 (not UNKNOWN).
2. Per page, start at 100.
3. Subtract 40 if zero H1 tags, or 25 if more than one H1.
4. Subtract min(30, Skips × 10), where a 'skip' is a jump of more than 1 heading level between consecutive headings.
5. Floor each page's score at 0; overall score = average of all per-page scores.
Note: Scores 0 outright (not UNKNOWN) if no headings are found on any page at all.
TECH-11:
1. Per qualifying page, start at 100.
2. Subtract 30 if words-per-heading > 220 (sections too long).
3. Subtract 20 if heading density (headings per 1000 words) < 1.5.
4. If a page has no headings at all → its score is set to 30.
5. Site score = mean of per-page scores.
6. If the LLM returns a usable total, the score is REPLACED with (LLM liftable count ÷ LLM total) × 100, and confidence rises from 0.7 to 0.8.
Note: Defaults to 40 if no pages qualify (word count <40). This is one of the few checks where the LLM can override the deterministic score rather than just annotate it; if the LLM call fails, the heuristic score stands.
TECH-12:
1. Score = 100 if tables + lists ≥ 8.
2. Score = 70 if tables + lists ≥ 3.
3. Score = 40 otherwise.
Note: Note: despite the registry description mentioning detection of 'image-based/table-like visuals,' the code performs no image analysis at all — it is purely a tiered count of semantic HTML elements.
TECH-13:
1. Per page, Ratio = Text length ÷ HTML length × 100.
2. Depth = 100 if word count ≥ 400, else (Word count ÷ 400) × 100.
3. Combined = Ratio × 0.4 + Depth × 0.6.
4. Score = min(100, average Combined across all pages).
Note: Defaults to 0 (not UNKNOWN) if there are no pages at all.
TECH-14:
1. If the site has zero images at all → Score = 80 (neutral baseline).
2. Usable images = alt text is non-empty, not a generic value ('image','img','logo'), and longer than 3 characters. Image score = Usable ÷ Total images × 100.
3. Video score = 100 if there are zero videos, else (Transcript-mentioning pages ÷ Videos) × 100, capped at 100.
4. Score = Image score × 0.7 + Video score × 0.3.
Note: Transcript presence is measured per page (any mention of the word 'transcript'), not matched to a specific video.
TECH-15:
Score = 60 + (Pages with a date ÷ Total pages) × 40.
Note: Every site gets a flat 60-point floor since dates matter less on non-article pages; there is no UNKNOWN case for this check.
TECH-16:
1. If no Organization item exists at all → Score = 0.
2. Present = however many of [name, url, logo, sameAs] have a truthy value (out of 4).
3. Score = (Present ÷ 4) × 80 + (20 if address or contact info is also present, else 0).
TECH-17:
1. Expected schema type by page_type: article→Article, service→Service, about→Organization, home→Organization; other page types have no expectation and are excluded.
2. A page 'matches' if its JSON-LD @types include the expected type (case-insensitive) or include 'FAQPage'.
3. Score = (Applicable pages that match ÷ Applicable pages) × 100.
Note: Defaults to 50 if there are no applicable pages at all (e.g. an entirely uncategorized crawl).
TECH-18:
1. Score = 80 if any author signal exists anywhere on the site, else 25.
2. Score is bumped to 95 if any collected signal includes a jobTitle field.
Note: This is a site-wide binary/tiered check, not a per-page ratio, despite the registry's documented 50/20/30 field-weighted split.
TECH-19:
Score = Valid JSON-LD blocks ÷ Total JSON-LD blocks × 100.
Note: Defaults to 40 if there are zero JSON-LD blocks anywhere on the site. Note: only parse validity is checked — the handler does not compare block content against visible page values despite the registry description implying it.
TECH-20:
1. Per page, start 'ok' = True.
2. If a canonical tag exists, flag not-ok only when the canonical's path differs from the final URL's path AND it has a distinct network location AND its path is not the site root/home page.
3. If no canonical tag exists at all → flag not-ok ('missing canonical').
4. If the page took ≥3 redirect hops to load → flag not-ok.
5. Score = (Pages marked ok ÷ Total pages) × 100.
TECH-21:
1. If no hreflang tags exist anywhere → Score = 100 (treated as a single-market site, Not Applicable rather than a fail).
2. If tags exist, Valid = tags with both a lang code and an href populated. Score = Valid ÷ Total tags × 100.
Note: Note: this checks tag completeness only — it does not verify true reciprocity between page pairs or locale-code correctness beyond presence, despite the registry description.
TECH-22:
1. Per page, title_ok = length 20-70 characters; desc_ok = length 70-170 characters.
2. Uniq_title = distinct non-empty titles ÷ non-empty titles (site-wide); Uniq_desc likewise for descriptions.
3. Presence = pages with both a title and description ÷ Total pages.
4. Length_quality = pages meeting both length ranges ÷ Total pages.
5. Score = Presence × 50 + Uniq_title × 15 + Uniq_desc × 10 + Length_quality × 25.
ON-02:
1. If there are no question-heading/answer pairs at all → Score defaults to 25 (not UNKNOWN).
2. Per answer, base quality = 70 if word count ≥20 ('direct'), else 30.
3. +30 if word count is between 40 and 80 (ideal window); else +15 if between 20 and 120. Cap at 100.
4. Overall score = average of all per-answer scores across the site.
Note: Defaults to 25 (a diagnostic fallback, not UNKNOWN) if no question-heading/answer pairs exist. Note: despite registry.json listing this as AI-assisted, the code contains no LLM call — it is purely a word-count/regex heuristic.
ON-03:
1. Take the site's own real service/category terms (derived dynamically from its nav menu and service-page titles, not a fixed word list).
2. For each term that appears on the site, check whether it is followed by a defining phrase (is/are/means/refers to/helps).
3. Score = (Terms defined ÷ Terms present) × 100; defaults to 30 if none of the site's terms were found in its own text.
4. If the AI reviewer is available, it re-judges each term's definition quality and its verdict REPLACES this score.
ON-04:
1. Take the first ~2 sentences of each of the first 12 pages as the "opening".
2. Generic = opening contains filler phrases ("welcome to", "in today's", "we are a leading", "leveraging cutting").
3. Specific = opening mentions the site's own brand name or one of its own real service categories (derived dynamically).
4. Per page: Score = 85 (specific, not generic), 55 (specific but also generic), or 35 (neither).
5. Overall = average across the 12 pages (defaults to 40 if no pages).
ON-05:
1. has_heading = any heading matches 'faqs?' or 'frequently asked'.
2. has_schema = any JSON-LD item typed 'FAQPage'.
3. Score = (Pages with has_heading OR has_schema ÷ Pages checked) × 100.
ON-06:
1. If no qualifying pages exist anywhere → Score defaults to 20.
2. Per qualifying page, schema = FAQ schema present (bool); visible = visible FAQ text present (bool).
3. Per-page contribution = 50 × schema + 50 × visible.
4. Score = average of per-page contributions across qualifying pages.
Note: Defaults to 20 if no qualifying pages (with FAQ schema or visible FAQ text) exist anywhere on the site.
ON-07:
1. If no pages are eligible → Score defaults to 40.
2. Score = (Eligible pages containing at least one <table> ÷ Eligible pages) × 100.
Note: Defaults to 40 if no pages are eligible for comparison at all.
ON-08:
1. A list counts as 'total' if not in nav/header/footer and has 2+ items.
2. A list is 'useful' if it has 3+ items AND its text contains any of step/how/benefit/includ/deliver/process.
3. Score = (Useful lists ÷ Total lists) × 100.
Note: Defaults to 35 if no qualifying lists exist on the site at all.
ON-10:
1. Per qualifying page, density = frequency of the most common word ÷ total words.
2. Average density = mean across all qualifying pages.
3. Score = 100 if average density < 0.025; 75 if < 0.04; otherwise 45.
ON-11:
1. Check each service page's text against 8 universal content dimensions — problem/need, approach/process, features, outcomes/benefits, audience/market, pricing/plans, proof/trust, contact/next-step — each matched against several everyday synonym words, not one fixed technical term.
2. Per page: Score = (Dimensions present ÷ 8) × 100.
3. Overall = average across all service pages.
ON-12:
Score = (Pages with at least one numeric token ÷ Total pages) × 100.
Note: Note: every page counts as 'major' in the current implementation (the eligibility filter is always true), and no originality or sourcing check is actually performed — any 2+ digit number anywhere counts, despite the registry description implying an originality check.
ON-13:
Score = 80 if any such author signal exists anywhere on the site, else 30.
Note: This is a single site-wide binary check, not a per-page or per-field completeness ratio, despite the registry's documented 'completeness score across required fields' description.
ON-14:
1. Per page: clients = matches client|customer|partner; numbers = matches a 2+ digit percentage or 'N+' pattern; deploy = matches deploy|implementation|production|rolled out.
2. Per-page score = Clients × 25 + Numbers × 30 + Deploy × 25 + (20 bonus if both clients and numbers are true).
3. Overall = average across all pages.
ON-15:
1. A sentence is a 'claim' if it has a 2+ digit number and more than 6 words.
2. A claim is 'sourced' if the page has an outbound link whose anchor text (first 40 characters) appears in that sentence, OR the sentence contains 'source', 'according to', or 'report'.
3. Score = (Sourced claims ÷ Total claims) × 100.
Note: Defaults to 35 if no claims exist anywhere on the site.
ON-16:
1. Hits = pages containing any reviewer-credit phrase.
2. Need = pages classified as 'article' or 'service'.
3. If any 'need' pages exist, Score = min(100, (Hits ÷ Need) × 100).
4. If there are no 'need' pages at all, Score = 60 if any hits exist anywhere, else 25.
ON-17:
Score = 50 + (Pages with a date ÷ Total pages) × 50.
Note: Note: no actual comparison against topic-specific 'shelf life' expectations is implemented, despite the registry description — presence of any date is the entire check.
ON-18:
1. Check every page for 6 universal buyer-journey stages: awareness, qualification, comparison, objection-handling, trust, and decision — each matched against everyday marketing/e-commerce phrases (the "comparison" stage also checks for "why [the site's own brand name]", added dynamically per site).
2. Score = (Stages with at least one covering page ÷ 6) × 100.
ON-19:
1. A page 'matches' if its URL + title fits the pattern.
2. Score = 80 if 3 or more matching pages exist; 45 if 1-2 exist; 15 if none exist.
Note: Note: registry marks this as requiring the LLM, but the code contains no LLM call — a single regex pattern drives the entire score.
ON-20:
1. A pair 'overlaps' if similarity ≥ 0.7 and the titles are not identical.
2. Score = 100 if no overlapping pairs exist.
3. Otherwise Score = max(40, 100 − 12 × number of overlapping pairs).
Note: Note: the registry mentions embeddings and an LLM confirmation step at similarity >0.85, but the implemented code uses only title-word Jaccard similarity — no embeddings and no LLM call.
ON-21:
1. Thin = non-utility pages with word count < 180.
2. Duplicate pair = two pages whose first-400-character word sets overlap with Jaccard ratio > 0.72.
3. Score = 100 − min(60, Thin count × 8 + Duplicate pair count × 10).
Note: Total deduction is capped at 60, giving an effective score floor of 40.
ON-22:
1. Take the site's own real service categories and real office locations (both derived dynamically from its own pages, plus a small set of universal reach words like "global"/"worldwide"/"nationwide" as a fallback) — never a fixed one-company list.
2. Per page: Brand = brand name present; Category = one of the site's own categories present; Geo = one of the site's own locations (or a reach word) present.
3. Score = (Pages where Brand AND Category AND Geo are ALL true ÷ Total pages) × 100.
OFF-01:
1. Search Wikidata for the site's own company name (found dynamically from the page, not fixed).
2. If the search fails → UNKNOWN.
3. Pick the best match: the first hit whose label/description contains the site's brand name, or a generic company word (company, business, corporation, organization, enterprise, firm); otherwise the first hit returned.
4. If there are no hits at all → Score = 0.
5. Score = 70 (match found) + 20 (if the match's own label contains the brand name) + 10 (if it has a description).
Maximum = 100.
OFF-02:
1. If the search fails → UNKNOWN.
2. If zero hits → Score = 20.
3. Heuristic 'about' match: any hit's title contains the first word of the company name → heuristic score 80, else 20.
4. If the LLM returns a usable verdict: when about_company is true, Score = 50 + Source authority × 0.3 + Entity accuracy × 0.2 (each defaults to 70 if the LLM omits them); when about_company is false, Score = 20.
5. Score capped at 100.
Note: On LLM failure, the substring-match heuristic score (80 or 20) is used instead.
OFF-05:
1. Read the company's real office locations from its own site (schema data or footer text) — not a fixed city list.
2. Search Wikidata for the site's own company name.
3. If that search fails → UNKNOWN.
4. Score = 70 if a Wikidata match exists and its label contains the site's brand name, else 40.
OFF-06:
1. Scan all page text for generic certification/accreditation language: "certified"/"accredited", "compliance"/"compliant", "licensed", any ISO standard number, or a "[X] partner" tier phrase (certified/authorized/gold/platinum/elite) — these patterns apply to any industry, not just IT vendor badges.
2. Score = 40 if no such claim is found.
3. Score = 55 if one or more claims are found (issuer is not independently verified, so this is capped at 55).
OFF-12:
1. If the search fails → UNKNOWN.
2. Score = 60 if hits ≥3; 30 if hits are 1-2; 15 if zero hits.
OFF-16:
1. Take the site's own top real service category (derived dynamically from its nav/service pages, not a fixed word).
2. Search: best [that category] "[company name]".
3. If the search fails → UNKNOWN.
4. Score = 50 if the brand name appears anywhere in the results, else 20.
